transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Start time: 09:42 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood CSM), Priya (Atlas Head of Procurement), Marcus (Atlas Legal), Samir (Atlas Security), Leah (Atlas Eng), Talia (Atlas FinOps)

Summary:
High-level alignment on legal DPA/MAA redlines, SLA tiers and pricing pathing for pilot to production. Deep dive on KMS options (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed) and implications for egress/xfer charges and latency. Agreed pilot scope and next steps to enable procurement sign-off.

Topics covered:
- DPA redline expectations and data residency
- SLA tiers (p95/p99, regional failover) and crediting model
- KMS: BYOK via customer HSM/KMS vs Redwood-managed keys and HSM escrow
- Pricing: committed dedicated capacity vs usage-based hosted pricing and egress fees
- Pilot scope, benchmarks, and timeline to procurement approval

Action items captured in metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): "Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we can see a full house — uh — thanks Priya, Marcus, Samir, Leah. We're planning to go 45 to 60 minutes, cover the DPA/MAA redlines, talk SLA tiers and KMS options and then land on pilot ask, is that right from Atlas side?"

[00:23] Priya (Atlas): "Yep, that's right. From procurement perspective we need to understand the DPA exposures, what SSO and keying options you support, and the pricing path to get this through our finance committee. We'll have some specific egress questions as well."

[00:40] Marcus (Atlas): "And legal wants to baseline the redlines today, we may not close everything but need a clear path. Also want to understand audit logs and retention policy, like retention for token-level metadata — that's key for us."

[01:05] Jonah (Redwood SE): "Great. I'll run through the KMS and infra options first, then Maya can speak to commercial. Apologies in advance for any audio blips — I have a spotty connection. So, two KMS patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys (we rotate keys, store in our KMS), 2) Customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM (BYOK). With BYOK, the plaintext never touches our persistent stores, and you control rotations and destroy. There's a small latency impact on cold-starts for key unwrap, usually in the low single-digit milliseconds per request, more noticeable with really short SLO windows."

[01:46] Samir (Atlas): "When you say 'low single-digit ms' on key unwrap, is that per token? Or per request? Our concern is at 1-2x token sizes for chat workloads, we can't have 100ms added at p99. What's the observed delta?"

[02:12] Jonah: "Good question. It's per request, so one unwrap per session bootstrap — not per token — because we cache unwrapped session keys for the KV cache. So the per-token path isn't redoing the unwrap. For longer-running sessions the impact is negligible. If you do very short TTLs for each call then you would see more calls, but our default is session caching for keys to avoid per-token crypto overhead."

[02:40] Leah (Atlas): "Okay that helps. We were worried it was per-token. Also, can you explain any implications on your Dedicated offering versus Hosted for BYOK?"

[02:56] Jonah: "Sure. On Dedicated, we can deploy a dedicated key broker in your VPC and integrate directly with your KMS/HSM — that removes cross-tenant surface area. For Hosted with BYOK, the customer metadata is still separate, but the key unwrap still happens at the edge of our boundary — we can supply an HSM gateway in the customer's cloud region to reduce egress and latency. There's documentation I'll share after this call."

[03:25] Marcus: "And about audit logs — can you produce tamper-evident logs that show key access event with principal, timestamp, and request id?"

[03:38] Jonah: "Yes — we provide an audit feed that includes key usage and admin events, with S3-compatible retention or to your SIEM via Kinesis/Event Hub. The logs can be routed to your tenant's log collector. They are not cryptographically signed by default, but we do offer signed log delivery for High Assurance packages. That said, we should capture Marcus' exact requirement as an action item."

[04:05] Talia (Atlas, FinOps): "On pricing, we have two internal lanes — a spend billable lane for early pilot and a committed lane for production. We need to understand the effective unit price both for hosted usage-based and for a Dedicated reserved capacity commit. Also what egress or region fees come into play."

[04:28] Maya (Redwood AE): "Totally. Our default pricing sheet has usage-per-token for hosted and month-based reserved units for Dedicated. A typical commit reduces per-token cost by around 30-55% depending on size and model family. Egress charges are a pass-through in some cases — if you want KMS in a private region or data residency controls, that can affect cost due to cross-region replication. We'll send an illustrative pricing worksheet with examples for Atlas' expected Q1 profile."

[04:55] Priya: "Can you clarify the SLA language — we're looking at p95 and p99 latency commitments, uptime percent, and the remedy/credit model. What does Redwood promise for failover between regions?"

[05:14] Rina (Redwood CSM): "We typically offer an SLA with 99.9% uptime for hosted and a 99.95% or higher for Dedicated depending on commit and configuration. Latency SLOs are negotiated — we commit to p95/p99 targets for specific model routes. For cross-region failover, we can provide automated routing policies and can commit to RTOs in the SLA with a phase-in testing requirement. The credit model is percentage-of-monthly-fee credits tied to duration and severity, similar to other infra providers. We'll produce the draft SLA language for Marcus to look at."

[05:50] Marcus: "We need clarity on whether the SLA includes third-party components and what constitutes 'downtime' specifically for inference (vs. control plane). Also, do you have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001?"

[06:05] Maya: "Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. The SLA differentiates between control plane and data plane; inference availability is covered but outages due to customer misconfiguration or force majeure are excluded. We'll mark the SLA draft to show exact carveouts."

[06:26] Samir: "One of our binding controls is that keys must be rotated every 90 days and retained in the customer's KMS. Is that supported?"

[06:36] Jonah: "Yes — we support rotation policies orchestrated by your KMS. The rotation can be automated or manual. If you rotate frequently, we recommend the Dedicated route or local HSM gateway to avoid repeated re-onboarding noise."

[06:56] Leah: "On the commercial path, what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated? And is there a pilot-to-prod conversion discount?"

[07:08] Maya: "Minimums vary by hardware profile, but we typically see 1-2 reserved GPU nodes as a small commit for Dedicated pilots. We offer a pilot conversion discount if you commit within the quarter after a successful pilot — we can bake that into the pricing worksheet. Talia, we can model a 12-month commit vs pay-as-you-go matrix."

[07:34] Talia: "Good, we'll need that matrix in time for our finance meeting on 2027-01-05. Can you get it to us by the 17th so we can factor into the formality pack?"

[07:46] Maya: "Yes, due 2026-12-17, noted."

[08:00] Jonah: "Switching to pilot scope — proposed: 2-week pilot, synthetic traffic plus a small shadow of production traffic, target 100k tokens/day, model family X (Llama-variant), measure p95/p99 latency, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll run a baseline run and a stressed run with KV cache cold starts, then iterate on batching and cache configs. That should give Atlas a predictable unit cost and performance profile."

[08:36] Leah: "100k tokens/day sounds reasonable for an initial pilot. We'll need to confirm whether we can route a slice of traffic and how quick the canary can be cut over in our infra. Also we need the benchmark template so we can ensure apples-to-apples measurements."

[08:55] Jonah: "I'll share a benchmark template — it includes sequence length distributions, prompt types, and synthetics for KV cache behavior. Also, we'll include instructions for capturing token-level cost and latency traces in the console and how to export them."

[09:14] Priya: "Commercially, procurement needs the DPA redline and a clear path for exceptions. Marcus will do initial redlines but we may ask for a legal-only sync next week. Also need the standard insurance and indemnity limits spelled out."

[09:32] Marcus: "Yes, we will prepare redlines. Two items to highlight: 1) Data deletion and retention obligations for training / model use — we need explicit non-use for training unless we opt in; 2) Escrow for keys if there's a custody transfer scenario."

[09:52] Maya: "We can explicitly carve out model training — Redwood does not train models on tenant data without explicit consent. For escrow, we offer options, including auditor escrow and HSM key wrapping for migration scenarios. We'll include language in the DPA/MAA."

[10:12] Marcus: "What about export controls and data residency? We have EU customers and need to keep EU data in-region."

[10:22] Jonah: "We support region pinning and data-at-rest residency options — Dedicated in-region is the straightforward option. For Hosted, we can place inference in an EU region for those routes; egress between regions is billable. We'll add explicit language showing where data can and cannot leave."

[10:42] Priya: "Ok — small administrative point: what's Redwood's process for DPA signature? Does legal sign the DPA first and MSA second? Any sequence we should follow?"

[10:54] Maya: "Typically we provide a DPA/MAA supplement alongside the MSA. Legal usually negotiates the DPA concurrently with MSA. For larger enterprises we offer a two-stage approach: a pilot addendum + full MSA on conversion, which seems to fit Atlas."

[11:12] Talia: "On FinOps, are there any hidden buckets — e.g., cache warm-up costs, KV prepopulation charges, or storage for audit logs?"

[11:24] Rina: "We have separate billing lines for storage (audit logs retention), network egress and optional cache snapshot costs. Cache warm-ups are typically within baseline compute for Dedicated; for Hosted, heavy prepopulation might be charged as a short-run compute spike on the invoice. Policy is to be transparent in the worksheet."

[11:45] Samir: "Also, we have to validate your key access controls with our third-party pen test team. How do we provide scoped access without exposing keys?"

[11:55] Jonah: "We can provide a read-only API key for telemetry and a separate audit-only credential. For key-handling validation, we support a restricted validation flow with faux keys in a staging environment. For on-prem or VPC deployments we can run the pen test with local HSM gating to avoid production key exposure."

[12:20] Marcus: "We may ask for an attestation around your KMS handling, e.g., paper trail for key deletion."

[12:28] Maya: "We can provide a KMS handling attestation and a summary of key lifecycle operations from our SOC reports."

[12:36] Leah: "If we do Dedicated, how long to provision cluster nodes in our VPC?"

[12:42] Jonah: "Typically 2-4 weeks depending on region and hardware availability — we can accelerate but it may involve an initial warm-up on hosted to run the pilot while we get Dedicated in place."

[12:58] Priya: "We're short on calendar — legal wants a 30-minute redline check next Thursday. Is that doable?"

[13:06] Marcus: "Next Thursday works for me. Suggest Marcus + Priya from Atlas, Maya + a Redwood counsel and Rina."

[13:15] Maya: "Works — I'll loop counsel in and book a 30-minute slot."

[13:20] Jonah: "One last technical note on latency v cost tradeoff: batching increases throughput and reduces per-token cost, but it can push tail latency up. For interactive chat we prefer smaller batch sizes and more KV caching; for high throughput batch inference you get better unit economics. We'll help tune."

[13:44] Leah: "We'll need your suggested initial batching and cache configs in the benchmark template."

[13:50] Jonah: "Will do."

[14:00] Rina: "Ok, to make sure we're aligned on next steps: Maya will send DPA + pricing, Jonah will share benchmark template and provision pilot env, Samir will share KMS requirements, Marcus will supply legal redlines, Leah will confirm traffic profile and integration owner, and Talia will share finance meeting date."

[14:25] Priya: "Yes, and procurement will need the pilot acceptance criteria so we can route to the finance committee after the pilot."

[14:35] Maya: "We'll include a short acceptance playbook with pass/fail metrics for pilot."

[14:40] Marcus: "One more question — indemnity caps and IP carveouts, we usually expect mutual indemnity and a reasonable cap tied to fees. Is Redwood open to that?"

[14:54] Maya: "Yes, mutual indemnities are standard; caps can be negotiated to be a multiple of fees or a fixed amount. We'll put Redwood's standard language in the MSA and Marcus can propose changes."

[15:10] Samir: "Any restrictions on scanning attachments or files? We do a lot of attachments and PII redaction is a must."

[15:20] Jonah: "We support content filtering and PII detection out of the box and you can configure masks or use a pre-ingest redaction pipeline. For PII-sensitive routes we recommend a dedicated route with tight RBAC and audit trails."

[15:38] Leah: "Ok that's helpful."

[15:45] Maya: "We have about 40 minutes left — want to go deeper anywhere?"

[15:51] Marcus: "I think legal will review drafts offline. Could we get the DPA and the SLA drafts in redline-friendly format? Word doc or track changes?"

[16:05] Maya: "Yes we'll send Word with tracked changes and a PDF summary."

[16:12] Priya: "One last procurement question: what is Redwood's normal lead time for initial invoice and Do you require prepayment for Dedicated?"

[16:24] Maya: "We issue an invoice at contract signature; for Dedicated we often require a partial upfront on the first invoice depending on term and hardware procurement lead times. We can put specific terms in the MSA."

[16:40] Talia: "If you require an upfront, send the exact % so finance can pre-clear it."

[16:46] Maya: "Will include in the pricing worksheet."

[17:00] Jonah: "I'll call out where hardware procurement can create a lag and options to start the pilot on-hosted while Dedicated is spun up."

[17:12] Priya: "Good."

[17:20] Maya: "Alright, wrapping. I'll confirm the legal-only slot for next Thursday, send DPA + pricing worksheet by 12/17, Jonah will share the benchmark template and pilot plan by 12/18. Marcus will return redlines by 12/22. Does that timeline work for Atlas?"

[17:38] Priya: "Yes, that works. One ask — please include sample SLA credit calculation so our procurement team can see expected credits for varying downtimes."

[17:48] Rina: "We'll include a sample table in the SLA draft."

[17:55] Marcus: "Ok look forward to the doc set."

[18:00] Maya: "Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to the security packet (https://redwood.example/security/atlas-packet.pdf), pricing worksheet, and the benchmark template."

[18:12] All: "Thanks, bye."

Notes / imperfections: occasional fill words and overlap in speakers; some product names were spoken quickly and auto-transcript changed 'KV cache' to 'K V cash' in a couple spots — flagged for manual review.
